title: SRE Weekly Update - 2026-10-17
summary: Weekly SRE summary covering a short degrading incident in us-west1 caused by an autoscaler regression, current SLO posture, on-call handoff notes, and action items for stabilization and test coverage.
body:
Highlights:
- Short degradation incident in us-west1 on 2026-10-15 affecting Redwood Hosted API (text-generation) — partial traffic saw elevated 5xxs and p95 latency spikes for ~15 minutes.
- Root cause identified as an autoscaler regression introduced in PR #4821 that caused a delayed scale-up window under a rare scheduling path. Patch rolled forward and verified.
- No data loss, no customer data exposure. Customer-impact summary sent to CS for the handful of affected enterprise tenants.

Incidents (INC-230):
- Timeline:
  - 2026-10-15 01:42 UTC: Pager triggered for elevated error rate (5xx) for hosted-api us-west1 – alert routed to primary on-call (Jasper).
  - 01:42–01:50 UTC: Initial triage; autoscaler logs show delayed node provisioning events and several timeouts to the provisioning API.
  - 01:52 UTC: Canary routing enabled to divert new requests to us-east1 until mitigation verified.
  - 02:00 UTC: Roll-forward of autoscaler patch (revert of regression path) deployed to us-west1; monitoring shows error rate returning to baseline by 02:08 UTC.
  - 02:15 UTC: Incident declared resolved; follow-up actions assigned.
- Impact:
  - Affected customers: ~6 heavy-hosted tenants experienced increased latency and ~0.8% spike in 5xx during window.
  - Duration: ~15–20 minutes of elevated errors; no sustained SLA breaches recorded, but partial burn of error budget for hosted-api in us-west1 for that hour.
- Communication:
  - Incident Slack channel (#sre-inc-230) used for coordination.
  - Customer Success notified via one-off emails to impacted accounts; CS has follow-up scheduled.

Root Cause & Fix:
- Root cause: A codepath introduced to optimize scale-down stability incorrectly short-circuited a scale-up warm-up path when a transient provisioning latency occurred. Under a rare combination (short burst + provisioning API tail latency), the autoscaler delayed requesting additional nodes until a timeout which was longer than our request timeout, resulting in backlog and 5xxs.
- Immediate fix: Roll-forward to stable autoscaler (PR 4821 reverted), added additional defensive checks to ensure scale-up path is prioritized when queue depth crosses threshold.
- Long-term: Additional tests and instrumentation (see Action Items).

SLO Posture:
- hosted-api (global): 99.9% availability SLA — current month at 99.95% (on track).
- hosted-api us-west1 (regional): noticed a small error budget burn for 2026-10-15 window. Regional p95 latency increased from baseline 120ms -> 480ms during incident.
- embeddings-api: no notable regressions.
- Ops note: We will update the SLO dashboard to include a new dimension for autoscaler-related incidents so we can correlate error budget burns to autoscaling events easily.

On-call Handoffs & Rotation:
- This week: Primary on-call: Jasper Nguyen; Secondary: Priya Rao; Tertiary: Liam O'Connell.
- Handoff notes for next week:
  - Primary -> Sofia Martinez (2026-10-19 08:00 UTC handoff)
  - Known risk windows: increased load expected 2026-10-20 00:00–06:00 UTC for demo traffic from partner Epsilon — watch autoscaler and provisioning metrics.
  - Current open pages for follow-up: INC-230 postmortem, SRE-421 (flaky provisioning API test), and incident runbook updates.

Action Items (owners):
- Add autoscaler unit + integration tests covering the short-circuit warm-up and provisioning latency path (owner: Priya Rao, due: 2026-10-24).
- Instrumentation: add a dedicated autoscaler metric for "scale_up_blocked_duration" and alert if any host experiences >30s blockage (owner: Liam O'Connell, due: 2026-10-21).
- Update runbooks: improve step-by-step mitigation checklist for provisioning API timeouts and add explicit rollback instructions (owner: Jasper Nguyen, due: 2026-10-22).
- Postmortem doc: draft and review (owner: Ariana Patel / Jasper Nguyen, link: INC-230 Confluence page, due: 2026-10-19).

Reliability Work & Deployments:
- Deployed: autoscaler rollback (stable) to us-west1 and canary to us-central.
- Rolling soon: improved provisioning client with exponential fallback (scheduled 2026-10-20, owner: infra team).
- Ongoing: SLO dashboard enhancements (perf-team) — ETA 2026-11-01.

Metrics Snapshot (weekly):
- Hosted API (global): p50 32ms, p95 120ms, error rate 0.04%
- Hosted API (us-west1) baseline pre-incident: p95 120ms; incident spike p95 480ms for 01:40–02:10 UTC 2026-10-15
- Avg provision latency (control plane -> instance up): baseline 18s; transient tail spikes observed at 46–72s during incident window.

Meeting Notes (SRE Sync 2026-10-16):
- Attendees: Ariana Patel, Jasper Nguyen, Priya Rao, Liam O'Connell, Sofia Martinez, Cara Lin (platform eng).
- Topics covered:
  - Incident review (INC-230) — immediate mitigation decisions and owner assignment.
  - Autoscaler telemetry gaps and proposed new metrics.
  - Upcoming partner demo traffic and capacity plan for us-west1.
  - Rollout schedule for provisioning client update and canary strategy.
- Decisions:
  - Prioritize autoscaler tests and instrumentation before provisioning client rollout.
  - Add a short window (10 minutes) of cross-region warm routing for partner demo to reduce blast radius.

Risks & Open Questions:
- Provisioning API tail latency sources: cloud provider investigation opened (SRE-421). Need provider correlation logs from provisioning team.
- Do we need a global warm pool for partner-configured customers to avoid this class of impact? Cost tradeoffs to be discussed with product.

Notes to Self / Informal:
- Reminder: coordinate with CS early if we detect any pattern that could affect large customers; small "bursty" incidents can still create escalations.
- Keep the incident channel threads archived and link PRs directly to postmortem to speed up reviews.

Attachments / Links:
- Postmortem draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/INC-2026-230-autoscaler-outage
- Rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/4821
- Jira: JIRA-INC-230, SRE-421

Next Week Goals:
- Close action items on autoscaler tests, metrics and runbook updates.
- Validate provisioning client rollout in staging with extended tail latency simulation.
- Finalize postmortem and share with leadership + CS.

If anything urgent comes up over the weekend ping primary/secondary on Slack and escalate to on-call follow steps in runbook.
